Investment Policy for Solid Waste
Postclosure and Corrective Action Trust
Fund
Policy

It is the policy of the City of Avalon (“City”) to invest public funds pertaining to the City’s Landfill and Solid Waste
Collection System in a manner that will provide maximum security for the City’s capital, while also meeting the cash
flow needs of the City relative to its participation in CalRecycle’s Solid Waste Postclosure and Corrective Action Trust
Fund (“State Trust Fund”). This policy conforms to all state and local law governing the investment of public funds and
aims to maximize return within an acceptable and defined level of risk.

Scope

This investment policy applies to the City’s establishment of a trust fund for landfill closure and postclosure costs
(“Local Trust Fund”) in compliance with CalRecycle’s State Trust Fund program, as well as to cover corrective action
and operating liabilities. This policy is intended to supplement and not replace any other City investment policies for
general operations or other specified purposes.

Fiscal Prudence (Government Code § 53600.3)

Investments shall be made with judgment and care, under circumstances then prevailing, which persons of prudence,
direction and intelligence exercise in the management their own affairs, not for speculation, but for investment,
considering the probable safety of their capital as well as the probable income to be derived.

The standard of prudence to be used by City officials responsible for the investment of public funds shall be the
“prudent investor” standard and shall be applied in the context of managing the portfolio of the Local Trust Fund.
Investment officers acting in accordance with written procedures and the investment policy and exercising due
diligence shall be relieved of personal responsibility for an individual’s security risk or market price changes, provided
deviations from expectations are reported in a timely fashion and appropriate action is taken to control adverse
developments.

Investment Objectives

Safety – The safety or risk associated with an investment refers to the potential loss of principal, accrued interest, or a
combination of these. The City seeks to mitigate credit risk by prequalifying and continuously monitoring financial
institutions with which it will do business and by careful scrutiny of the credit worthiness of the investment
instruments as well as the institutions. Such resources as FDIC bank ratings, Sheshunoff, Fitch, Moody’s, and Standard
and Poor’s rating services may be utilized for this review. The City seeks to mitigate interest rate risk through
diversification of instruments as well as maturities.

Liquidity – The City’s investment portfolio will be structured with sufficient liquidity to allow the City to meet its
anticipated cash requirements. This will be accomplished through diversity of instruments to include those with active
secondary markets, those which match maturities to expected cash needs, and the State Local Agency Investment
Fund (LAIF) with immediate withdrawal provisions.

Yield – A competitive market rate of return is the third objective of the City’s investment program after the
fundamental requirements of safety and liquidity have been met.

Receipts for confirmation of purchase of authorized securities should include the following information: trade date,

Safekeeping of Securities

In accordance with Government Code Section 53601, all securities owned by the City shall be held in safekeeping by
the City's custodial bank or a third party bank trust department, acting for the City under the terms of a custody
agreement. All securities will be received and delivered using standard Delivery Versus Payment procedures, which
ensures that securities are deposited with the third party custodian prior to release of funds. A third party custodian, as
evidenced by safekeeping receipts, will hold securities. Investments in LAIF or money market mutual funds are
undeliverable and are not subject to delivery or third party safekeeping.

Diversification

The City will diversify its investments by security type and institution. Except for US Treasury securities and authorized
pools (LAIF and LACIP), no more than 50% of the entity's total investment portfolio will be invested in a single security
type or with a single financial institution.

Maximum Maturities

To the extent possible, the City will attempt to match its investments with anticipated cash flow requirements. Unless
matched to a specific cash flow and authorized by the Government Code, the City will not directly invest in securities
matured more than five (5) years from the date of purchase.

Internal Control

The Treasurer shall establish an annual process of independent review by an external auditor. This review will provide
assurances on internal controls through compliance with policies and procedures.

Performance Standards

The investment portfolio will be designed to obtain the highest rate, with the greatest security and liquidity, consistent
with the cash flow requirements of the City, but at no less rate on the date of investment than the rate being paid by
the Local Agency Investment Fund (LAIF).

Reporting

Credit Card Purchasing Policy
Purpose:

The purpose of the policy is to establish a framework for the appropriate use of City-issued credit cards. The use of City-
issued credit cards is intended to streamline small dollar purchases, reduce the acquisition period, reduce requests for
employee reimbursements, and minimize the use of personal credit cards for City-related expenses. Employees with
City-issued credit cards (Card Users) must also adhere to the City’s Procurement Policy, as outlined in the Avalon
Municipal Code, as well as the City’s Travel and Expense Reimbursement Policy.

Background:

The City utilizes credit cards for the procurement of goods for administrative convenience and efficiency. The City’s
credit card is managed by the Finance Department. The Finance Director, or their designee, is responsible for the
issuance, activation, cancellation, and payment of the credit card. Additionally, the Finance Department reviews the
documentation of credit card usage for compliance with the Credit Card Purchasing Policy with final approval by the
Finance Director.

Policy:

Purchases made by credit card must adhere to the City’s Procurement Policy, as outlined in the Avalon Municipal
Code Title 3, Chapter 4, and with the City’s Travel and Expense Reimbursement Policy.

Credit cards may be issued to City of Avalon department heads and their designees, as approved by the City Manager.
Credit cards shall not be issued to City Council Members, members of boards, committees, or commissions, volunteers,
part-time employees, seasonal employees, or contracted employees. Prior to card issuance, employees will also be
required to sign the cardholder agreement (Attachment A), indicating that they understand and accept the terms of
the policy.

City credit cards may not be used for the following:

  1. Cash advances
  a. Personal transactions unrelated to official City business
  b. Transactions beyond established credit limits
  c. Purchases that circumvent or violate City policies, finance policies, or exceed budgetary limits for the
  category of expense
  d. Purchases unauthorized or unlawful under federal and state laws, including but not limited to, ethical rules
  related to gifts and reporting obligations of elected officials
  e. Purchases deemed unauthorized or out of compliance with other applicable provisions of City of Avalon
  policies

Within five business days of receiving the credit card statement, card users must submit to the Finance Department
detailed receipts and descriptions of all credit card statement transactions, listing the business purpose, attendees,
date of purchase merchant’s name and budgeted account codes. If the card user does not have the proper
documentation for a transaction, an explanation shall be provided in the form of a memo countersigned by the card
user’s supervisor that includes a description of the item, business purpose, attendees, date of purchase, merchant’s
name budgeted account codes, and the reason why the documentation is missing.

Card Users shall take necessary measures to prevent unauthorized charges against the card. If the credit card is lost or
stolen, the Card User shall immediately report the occurrence to the Finance Director so that the card may be
cancelled. The Finance Department will coordinate with the Card User and the credit card issuer in handling all
